--- license: mit library_name: transformers pipeline_tag: image-text-to-text --- # DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017

Technical Report 👁️

## Introduction **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017** is a minor update to [**DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash**](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), delivering substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. Alongside these gains, the model reduces task execution time and output length, enabling users to complete tasks faster and at lower cost and advancing the performance–cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses.
| Benchmark | DS-V4.1-Flash-1017 | DS-V4.1-Flash | K3 | GLM-5.3 | GPT-5.6 Sol | Opus 5 | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | HLE w/o tools | 42.6 (44.0†) | 36.8 (39.1†) | 43.5 | 42.0† | 44.5 | 56.3 | | Terminal-Bench 4.0 | 42.3 | 31.2 | 12.6 | 37.9 | 39.9 | 51.8 | | DeepSWE v1.1 | 77.0 | 74.2 | 67.5 | 66.9 | 73.0 | 74.0 | | ProgramBench | 29.1 | 20.3 | 17.5 | 19.0 | 23.0 | 37.0 | | NL2Repo-Bench | 68.2 | 65.4 | 58.0 | 58.0 | 56.8 | 75.3 | | Automation-Bench v1.0.6 | 60.5 | 54.8 | 46.7 | 48.8 | 45.8 | 50.3 | | Agents’ Last Exam | 35.4 | 31.8 | 27.6 | 28.5 | 26.7 | 28.6 | | Apex Bench v1.1 | 72.1 | 64.6 | 47.8 | 56.6 | 54.3 | 65.8 | | Chartography (w/tools) | 83.0 | 78.9 | 68.1 | — | 79.9 | 84.0 | | BabyVision (w/tools) | 92.5 | 89.6 | 85.7 | — | 88.9 | 94.1 | | ZeroBench-main (w/tools) | 51.0 | 49.0 | 41.0 | — | 53.0 | 52.0 |
*† denotes the text-only subset of HLE. We use the Claude Code harness for Terminal-Bench 4.0 and the Mini-SWE-V2 harness for DeepSWE v1.1.* ## Prompt Encoding This release does not include a Jinja-format chat template. The [`encoding`](encoding/README.md) folder contains a self-contained Python reference implementation (`encoding.py`) with test cases for multi-turn conversations, tool calling, thinking mode, numeric reasoning effort, mid-conversation system messages, and interleaved image content. For production use, we additionally release [deepseek-recipe](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe), a set of Rust libraries with Python bindings that provides the same prompt format as a maintained, protocol-aware toolkit. It converts Messages, Chat Completions, and Responses API requests into the Conversation format, encodes them into DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 prompts or token IDs, and parses model output back into complete or streamed responses — covering thinking, tool calls, images, and generation settings. Model inference, tool execution, and HTTP transport are left to the caller. ## Minimal Inference Please refer to the [`inference`](inference/README.md) folder for instructions on weight conversion and running inference locally. **Recommended sampling parameters:** | Parameter | Value | | :--- | :--- | | `temperature` | 1.0 | | `top_p` | 1.0 | | `context_window` | 1M tokens | | `max_tokens` | ≥ 256K | ## License This repository and the model weights are licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{deepseekai2026deepseekv41flash, title={DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression}, author={DeepSeek-AI}, year={2026}, } ``` ## Contact If you have any questions, please raise an issue or contact us at [service@deepseek.com](mailto:service@deepseek.com).

# LFM3-1.7B LFM3-1.7B is a **text model for local agents and specialized applications**, based on our new tri-hybrid architecture. - **Agentic training:** post-trained for agentic harnesses such as Hermes Agent, Pi, and OpenClaw, with a 256K-token context window. - **Designed for the edge:** at 4-bit precision, it takes about 1 GB of memory, so it fits on any phone or laptop. - **Made to be specialized:** adapt the model to your domains, formats, and tools via quick single-GPU fine-tuning. Find more information about the LFM3 family in [our release blog post](https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm3). ## Model details
The [LFM3 family](https://huggingface.co/collections/LiquidAI/lfm3) includes base, text, vision, audio, omni, and decision models.

Checkpoint Post-trained, text-only language model
Parameters 1.73B
Architecture 24 layers: 13 gated short convolutions, 5 sliding-window attention, 6 global attention
Context length 256K tokens (input + output)
Vocabulary 128,000 tokens
Languages English, Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish, Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian, Hindi, Russian, Polish

![Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe overview: one speech LLM transcribes a recording in the style selected by the instruction](hero.png) **Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight, offline speech and audio model** for transcription in 40 languages, with support for recordings up to one hour and a 65,536-token context. Its hybrid mixture-of-experts architecture activates approximately **4.3B parameters**, including the audio encoder, and it is released in [BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B), [FP8](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-FP8), and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-NVFP4) precision. Table of contents - [Model Summary](#model-summary) - [Results at a Glance](#results-at-a-glance) - [Efficiency](#efficiency) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Prompt Guide](#prompt-guide) - [Model Architecture](#model-architecture) - [Language Support Matrix](#language-support-matrix) - [Training, Testing, and Evaluation Datasets](#training-testing-and-evaluation-datasets) - [Benchmark Results](#benchmark-results) - [Inference Setup and Prompts](#inference-setup-and-prompts) - [Ethical Considerations](#ethical-considerations)

# Model Overview ### Description NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe is an offline speech and audio model that processes recordings, together with text instructions and optional context, into text responses. NVIDIA developed this [Speech-Augmented Language Model (SALM)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09424) for multilingual transcription, speech translation, contextual transcription, speaker-attributed transcription, rich transcription, timestamp prediction, language identification, and audio question answering. The training mixture also includes a small amount of text instruction following and PII tagging/redaction tasks. This model is ready for commercial or non-commercial use. ### Model Summary | | | |:---|:---| | **Total Parameters** | 34B (4.3B active), including the audio encoder | | **Architecture** | Mamba-2–Transformer hybrid Mixture of Experts language model with a Parallel Expert Encoder (Transformer ASR encoder and speaker encoder) | | **Precision** | BF16 (full-precision reference weights); [FP8](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-FP8) and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-NVFP4) variants are available | | **Context Length** | 65,536 tokens; recordings up to 1 hour | | **Inputs / Outputs** | A

# 1. Introduction In Nanbeige4.3, we take a foundational step toward pushing the boundaries of lightweight agents. Our strategy centers on building a high-capacity teacher agent first, which will subsequently anchor the distillation of advanced agentic capabilities into smaller models. To this end, we first introduce Nanbeige4.3-33B, designed as the flagship teacher model for the Nanbeige4.3 series. Delivering state-of-the-art agentic performance among open models in the ~30B parameter class, Nanbeige4.3-33B excels at complex coding and professional cowork tasks. It not only offers a powerful, cost-effective option for immediate real-world deployment, but also lays the necessary foundation to power our upcoming small model distillation pipeline (e.g., for Nanbeige4.3-3B).

# Mistral Large 4 - Le Chonk

Mistral Large 4 is our largest and most capable model to date: a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 49 billion active parameters per token (52 billion including embeddings and output layers), trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own datacenters in Europe.

Mistral Large 4 unifies instruction following, reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows in a single set of weights. While a generalist model, it shows especially good performance on workloads such as cybersecurity, finance, and law, and it surpasses frontier closed models on visual grounding. It is natively fluent in 160+ languages, including every official language of the European Union.

Find more information on our [blog](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/). The model is also served on the [Mistral API](https://docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-large-4-0) as `mistral-large-4`.

> [!Note]
> The checkpoint ships with an embedded DSpark speculative decoding draft head — see [Speculative decoding (DSpark)](#speculative-decoding-dspark).

> [!Note]
> A quantized [NVFP4 checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B-NVFP4) is also available, with a smaller memory footprint, faster inference and same performance. It targets Blackwell GPUs and supports vLLM and SGLang.

## Key Features

Mistral Large 4 includes the following architectural choices:

- **~1T total / ~52B active parameters**: granular Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts (4 active per token) and 1 shared expert.
- **1M context length**, for long-context workloads.
- **Multimodal input**: accepts text and image input, with text output. Pixtral-style vision encoder trained to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios.
- **Instruct and Reasoning functionalities** with function calls, reasoning effort configurable per request.

Mistral Large 4 offers the following capabilities:

- **Reasoning Mode**: three reasoning efforts — `low`, `medium`, `high` (default) — so the same model can answer a quick chat reply or work through a complex agentic run.
- **Vision**: analyzes images, charts, technical drawings, and documents, with state-of-the-art visual grounding among open weights.
- **Multilingual**: natively fluent in 160+ languages, including all official languages of the European Union.
- **System Prompt**: strong adherence and support for system prompts.
- **Agentic**: native function calling, JSON output, and strict JSON schema enforcement.
- **Cybersecurity**: state of the art among open-weight models for security work, while refusing malicious requests.
- **Large Context Window**: supports a 1M context window.

We release this model under the [**Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License**](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B/blob/main/LICENSE): a modified version of the MIT license, for both commercial and non-commercial use — operating a Model-as-a-Service business requires a separate commercial license with Mistral.

## Recommended Settings

- **Reasoning Effort**:
  - `'low'` / `'medium'` / `'high'` — default is `'high'`.
  - Use `reasoning_effort="high"` for complex prompts and agentic usage, `'low'` for fast chat replies and `'medium'` for day to day usage.
- **Sampling**: for all reasoning efforts, we recommend the following sampling parameters:
  - `temperature=1.0`
  - `top_p=0.95`
- **System Prompt**: define a clear environment and use case, including guidance on how to effectively leverage tools in agentic systems.
- **Tools**: keep the set of tools well-defined and limit their number to the minimum required for the use case.
- **Context**: the checkpoint supports a 1M context window.

## Benchmarks

We compared Mistral Large 4 with recent open-weight models. We report results on agentic coding and global intelligence here; for more benchmarks, especially on cybersecurity, finance and law, see our [blog post](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/).

### Agentic Coding

Mistral Large 4 delivers frontier coding performance with significantly fewer tokens, making sophisticated coding agents more economical to run at scale.

On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, ML4 scores **48%**, effectively tied with the leading open-weight model, GLM-5.3, while using **47%** fewer tokens per task on average.

![Artificial Analysis - Coding Agent Index](images/coding_index.png)

### Global Intelligence

On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, Mistral Large 4 scores **26**, the highest among western open-weight models. The leading open-weight models from China score higher on this aggregate index, but Mistral Large 4 is particularly strong on coding and cybersecurity, as shown in our [blog post](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/).

![Artificial Analysis - Intelligence Index v5](images/intelligence_index.png)

## Demo Gallery

[Le Chonk Gallery](https://mistralai-ml4-le-chonk-gallery.hf.space/) is a live gallery of demo Spaces built with Mistral Large 4, from us and from the community: coding, vision and grounding, tool calls, JSON schema, multilingual, and more. Any Space tagged `Le_chonk` appears there.

Official demos run on the Mistral API with a small shared free budget per visitor for the first week of the release, so you can try the model without paying. You can also use your own Mistral API key.

To build a demo, we recommend [Mistral Vibe](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe), our coding agent powered by Mistral Large 4.

## Usage

You can find Mistral Large 4 support on multiple libraries for inference and fine-tuning.

We **thank** all the ecosystem folks who helped us throughout this release to integrate Le

Unlimited OCR Works 2

Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing.

## Release - [2026/10/28] Thanks to the [ms-swift community](https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift) for supporting training of **Unlimited OCR 2**. - [2026/10/27] 📊 We release [**MarathonDocBench**](https://huggingface.co/datasets/baidu/MarathonDocBench), a new benchmark for ultra-long document parsing. - [2026/10/27] 🤝 Thanks to the [ModelScope community](https://github.com/modelscope) for their support. Our model is now available at [ModelScope](https://modelscope.cn/models/PaddlePaddle/Unlimited-OCR-2). - [2026/10/27] 🤝 Thanks to the Baidu Cloud team for their support. Our model is now available on [Baidu Cloud](https://cloud.baidu.com/doc/OCR/s/fmr1p39gb). - [2026/10/27] 🤝 Thanks to [AK](https://x.com/_akhaliq) for creating a new demo for us. Try it at [Unlimited-OCR-2](https://huggingface.co/spaces/baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2). - [2026/10/27] 🚀 We release [**Unlimited OCR 2**](https://github.com/baidu/Unlimited-OCR), achieving unlimited-horizon parsing with SR-SWA. - [2026/07/21] 🤝 Thanks to the [ms-swift community](https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift) for their support, our model now supports training with [ms-swift](https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift). - [2026/07/03] 🤝 Thanks to the Baidu Cloud team for their support. Our model is now available on [Baidu Cloud](https://cloud.baidu.com/doc/OCR/s/fmr1p39gb). - [2026/06/28] 🤝 Thanks to the [vLLM community](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) and [Tianyu Guo](https://github.com/gty111) for their support, our model now supports vLLM inference. - [2026/06/24] 🤝 Thanks to [AK](https://x.com/_akhaliq) for creating a demo for us. It is now available at [Hugging Face Spaces](https://huggingface.co/spaces/baidu/Unlimited-OCR). - [2026/06/23] 📄 Our paper is now available on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23050). - [2026/06/23] 🤝 Thanks to the [ModelScope community](https://github.com/modelscope) for their support. Our model is now available at [ModelScope](https://modelscope.cn/models/PaddlePaddle/Unlimited-OCR). - [2026/06/22] 🚀 We present [Unlimited-OCR](https://github.com/baidu/Unlimited-OCR/tree/UnlimitedOCR1.0), aiming to push [Deepseek-OCR](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR) one step further. ## What's New in 2 * Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA): Compresses text-visual attention interactions from ultra-long sequences down to a fixed-size set of working references (e.g., 512 tokens). This bounds computational complexity, keeping per-step decoding latency and memory footprint nearly constant regardless of document length. * From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing: Powered by SR-SWA, Unlimited-OCR 2 achieves true, unbounded document parsing within a finite context window—effectively eliminating quadratic attention scaling and memory bottlenecks as documents grow. * Ultra-Long Document Parsing SOTA: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across both dozens-of-pages benchmarks (e.g., MPDocBench) and extreme hundred-page benchmarks (e.g., MarathonDocBench).
## Inference > Unlimited OCR 2 supports **Transformers** (native, for quick tests) and **SGLang** (recommended for serving). ### Transformers Tested with Python 3.10, `torch==2.13.0`, `transformers==4.52.1`, `huggingface-hub==0.36.0`, `tokenizers==0.21.4`, on an NVIDIA A800-80GB: ```shell pip install torch==2.13.0 torchvision pillow transformers==4.52.1 huggingface-hub==0.36.0 \ tokenizers==0.21.4 addict==2.4.0 einops==0.8.2 easydict==1.13 ``` Load the model once: ```python import torch from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer model_name = "baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2" tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=True) model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=True, use_safetensors=True, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).eval().cuda() ``` **Multi-page inference** (`infer_multi`). All pages of a document are parsed in one request, so the model can use cross-page context. Pass the page images in page order: ```python pages = [f"your_doc/page_{i}.jpg" for i in range(1, 8)] text, num_tokens = model.infer_multi(tokenizer, image_files=pages, output_path="output/multi", save_results=True) ``` The prompt is built automatically as `"" * num_pages + "Multi page parsing."`, and each page is encoded as one global view (base mode). --- license: apache-2.0 base_model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B base_model_relation: finetune datasets: - ccore/ThreeJS-3D-Scenes tags: - qwen3_5 - code - threejs - 3d - preview --- # Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder ### Early preview · General coding with a focus on 3D **An experiment exploring the feasibility of small language models for general-purpose coding and high-quality 3D scene generation.** This is an early preview of a 4B model I am still training, with a particular focus on creating interactive 3D scenes with Three.js. Initial hands-on results have been promising for coding in general, and especially for generating 3D scenes, so I decided to share the progress while development continues. This is an **independent fine-tune** by [CCORE](https://huggingface.co/ccore), based on [Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B). **It is not an official Qwen release.** ## Optional vision support — October 30, 2026 The **Q4_K_M and Q8_0 GGUF versions can also accept image inputs** when loaded with the original Qwen3.5-4B vision encoder/projector. You can attach a reference image and ask the model to generate a Three.js scene from it. [**Download the optional BF16 vision projector**](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/resolve/main/mmproj-Qwen3.5-4B-BF16.gguf?download=true) — approximately **644 MiB**. Download it once; the same file is used with either GGUF quantization. ### Image-guided Three.js example With a reference image attached and the Three.js system prompt below, the user prompt was simply: ```text create this scene using voxels 3d ```
Input referenceGenerated Three.js scene
The reference image was supplied in [community discussion #9](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/discussions/9); credit for the reference belongs to its original creator. The right-hand image is a screenshot of the generated scene. This is a qualitative example of image-guided generation; the output interprets the reference and does not reproduce every detail. ### Load the GGUF with vision in llama.cpp Download a model GGUF and the projector, then load both files explicitly: ```bash llama-server \ -m Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder-Q4_K_M.gguf \ --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3.5-4B-BF16.gguf \ --n-gpu-layers all --flash-attn on \ --ctx-size 65536 --parallel 1 ``` Open the server's WebUI, attach an image, and send your prompt. The setup was tested locally with **llama.cpp b11889**. For Q8_0, change the model filename to `Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder-Q8_0.gguf`; `--cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0` can reduce KV-cache memory use and was tested locally with vision at a configured 64K context. These were short tests, not full-context stress tests. The projector uses additional memory when loaded, and image tokens share the context window with the prompt and generated code. Image support in other frontends depends on their multimodal implementation. **Projector provenance:** this is the unmodified BF16 projector from [lmstudio-community/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/lmstudio-community/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF/tree/f9f88ac3e234be915e23811a6d28ea287bdb927e), based on [Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B), released under Apache 2.0. It is an optional companion file for the existing GGUF weights. ## Technical report — now available The **technical report for this training experiment is now available**. [**Read the technical report (PDF)**](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/blob/main/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder_Technical_Report.pdf) · [**Download the PDF**](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/resolve/main/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder_Technical_Report.pdf?download=true) ## Full FP16 weights — now available The **original FP16 weights** are now available in this repository in **Safetensors format**, alongside the Q4_K_M and Q8_0 GGUF versions. The release includes all **four weight shards**, the model configuration, tokenizer, generation configuration, chat template, and image/video processor settings. The FP16 weights were verified locally for **loading and text generation with Transformers 5.20.2**. The FP16 generation defaults use **temperature 0.6**, **top-k 20**, **top-p 0.95**, and **repetition penalty 1.0**, with caching enabled. [**Browse the FP16 files and GGUF versions**](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/tree/main) ## Training dataset — now available The dataset used to train this model is now public: [**CCORE Three.js 3D Scenes**](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ccore/ThreeJS-3D-Scenes). It contains **4,146 scene examples** (**3,933 training / 213 validation**), including prompts, full thinking traces, complete HTML/JavaScript responses, and complexity levels. Rendered reference images are available in the optional `previews` configuration. The dataset is released under the **MIT License**. ## October 27 checkpoint update Both **Q4_K_M** and **Q8_0** now contain the updated October 27 checkpoint.   text: 'Image 1 is the exact two players, outfits, frog mask, table-tennis table and drained pool: keep them exactly

    A fast table-tennis rally, shot with exactly these camera moves:

    00:00–00:03 — top-down from directly overhead, as in Image 1, as the rally begins and the ball flicks back and
    forth.

    00:03–00:06 — a smooth crane straight down from overhead to table height, ending right beside the net as the
    ball zips across.

    00:06–00:09 — fast whip pans left and right following the ball across the net, from one player to the other.

    00:09–00:12 — a 180-degree orbit around the frog-masked player as she leaps and smashes the ball.

    00:12–00:15 — a low-angle dolly backward along the pool floor as the woman in the red tracksuit dives and misses;
    the frog raises both arms and does a little victory dance; the camera settles and holds.

    The players, table and pool stay consistent and in the same place throughout. Photoreal 35mm film look, true
    colour, light natural grain, matching Image 1. SPEED IS CRITICAL: everything moves at normal real-time speed,
    like 24fps footage played back at 24fps - natural motion, NO slow motion.

    Sound: the quick tock-tock of the ball, sneakers squeaking on concrete, the smash, a thud as she dives, echo
    in the empty pool, the frog''s muffled cheer. Music: a funky, upbeat drum-and-bass groove.'

- example_title: A journey between balconies
  text: 'A tall white modernist apartment tower against a soft pale-blue sky with faint streaky cirrus cloud. The
    building sits on the right half of the frame; the left half is open sky. Smooth off-white render facade with
    small square windows in thick white frames. Three identical cantilevered concrete balconies are stacked vertically
    on the building''s corner, each a thick white slab with an angled, wedge-shaped underside and a thin white metal
    railing of vertical balusters. Crisp, graphic, minimal, soft 1970s film palette: chalky whites, powder blue,
    muted pastels.


    Three people are doing a slow, calm morning stretch routine, one per balcony. They are always gently in motion,
    never frozen, but every movement is slow, smooth and controlled, like yoga or tai chi: each stretch takes three
    to four seconds to flow into, eases gently at the end, and flows unhurried into the next. No fast, jerky, snapping
    or flailing movements. Graceful, deliberate, meditative.

    Top balcony: a young woman with dark hair pulled back, in a lilac fluffy knit jumper and matching lilac wide-leg
    knit trousers. She slowly reaches both arms high overhead, then gradually leans her upper body into a long side
    bend to the left, eases back to centre, and slowly leans to the right.

    Middle balcony: a man with short dark hair in a rust-red tracksuit. He hangs in a deep forward fold with palms
    on the floor, then slowly rolls up through his spine to standing, and lifts his arms in one wide, slow circle
    overhead.

    Bottom balcony: an older woman with short silver-grey hair in a cobalt blue short-sleeved polo and loose cream
    trousers. She holds a wide warrior lunge with arms stretched out to each side, slowly shifts her weight from
    one bent knee to the other, and gently sweeps one arm up and over her head into a side bend.

    Each person moves at their own unhurried rhythm, slightly out of sync with each other, with full-body range
    of motion: knitwear and trousers stretching and settling, real balance and weight.


    Camera, one continuous shot with no cuts:

    0-3s: Wide establishing frame. The camera begins a slow, smooth orbit around the corner of the tower, arcing
    about 40 degrees, with strong parallax between the balconies, building face and sky.

    3-5s: Still moving, the camera pushes in hard on the middle balcony until the man in the red tracksuit fills
    the frame alone, waist-up, mid-stretch, railing in the foreground.

    5-7s: A steady vertical boom up the face of the building, past the concrete underside of the slab above, revealing
    the lilac woman mid-side-bend.

    7-10s: A fast, controlled boom straight down past the middle balcony to the bottom one, revealing the older
    woman shifting through her lunge.

    10-13s: Smooth pull back and reverse orbit, landing on the opening wide composition, all three still actively
    stretching.


    Soft diffused daylight, gentle soft shadows under each slab, no hard sun. 35mm film look with fine grain. Stabilized
    crane/drone motion, never jittery.


    Sound: natural diegetic location sound only — light wind gusting past the building, distant city hum, faint
    birds, soft fabric rustle. No music, no score, no singing, no melody, no rhythm track. No speech, no voices,
    no talking, no dialogue, no murmuring, no vocal sounds of any kind.'

# FLUX 3 Image Klein for ComfyUI

![Launch gallery](./launch-gallery.jpg)

FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6B open weights model for text-to-image generation and image editing. It takes a prompt and up to 10 reference images and returns one image. Text-to-image, single-reference edits and multi-reference compositions run through the same model, with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct as the text encoder.

The 5.6B parameter label refers to the image transformer; the text encoder is separate.

This repository holds the model files repackaged for [ComfyUI](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI): the distilled and base transformers in BF16, int8 and NVFP4, the text encoder in BF16 and int8, the prompt upsampler in BF16, int8 and w4a8, and the image autoencoder. The original model repositories are [FLUX 3 Image Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein), [FLUX 3 Image Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) and [FLUX 3 Image Klein Prompt Upsampler](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup).

Inference code, prompt upsampling and the bounding box format: [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) on GitHub.

**Do not use the model without a prompt upsampler.** FLUX 3 Image Klein takes full scene captions, for text-to-image, editing and layout with boxes alike; a short prompt sent as typed gives generic output. Use ours, the `qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_int8_convrot.safetensors` file in this repository, which the workflows run by default (see [Using with ComfyUI](#using-with-comfyui)), or any LLM you prefer with a system prompt that expands the request into one full scene caption ([`system_prompts.json`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup/blob/main/system_prompts.json) has ours).

| Checkpoint | Format | Steps | Guidance | Built for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) | undistilled, bfloat16 | 50 | 3.5 | fine-tuning, LoRA training, research |
| [Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) | distilled, bfloat16 | 16 | none | generation and editing, self-hosting; the checkpoint behind the BFL API |

## Key Features

1. Text-to-image, single-reference editing and multi-reference generation in one model.
2. Bounding boxes in the prompt. Place elements with boxes on a 0 to 1000 grid, then recolor, move, replace or remove them through the prompt. Boxes guide placement and scale; they do not constrain pixels to a hard mask.
3. Text rendering within generated images.
4. Released under the [FLUX Kommunity License](LICENSE.md). The license permits non-commercial use and provides a commercial-output exception for Qualifying Users, subject to its terms. See [License](#license) below.

## Files

Place the files in the following folders:

```
📂 ComfyUI/
└── 📂 models/
    ├── 📂 diffusion_models/
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-base-bf16.safetensors
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-base-int8-convrot.safetensors
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-base-nvfp4.safetensors
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-bf16.safetensors
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-int8-convrot.safetensors
    │   └── flux3-image-klein-nvfp4.safetensors
    ├── 📂 text_encoders/
    │   ├── qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_bf16.safetensors
    │   ├── qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_int8_convrot.safetensors
    │   ├── qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_w4a8.safetensors
    │   ├── qwen3vl_4b_bf16.safetensors
    │   └── qwen3vl_4b_int8_convrot.safetensors
    └── 📂 vae/
        └── flux2-vae.safetensors
```

Files with `-base-` in the name are the base checkpoint; the others are the distilled checkpoint.

| File | Content | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-bf16.safetensors` | Klein, distilled, BF16 | 11.1 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-int8-convrot.safetensors` | Klein, distilled, int8 | 5.8 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-nvfp4.safetensors` | Klein, distilled, NVFP4 | 5.3 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-base-bf16.safetensors` | Klein Base, BF16 | 11.1 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-base-int8-convrot.safetensors` | Klein Base, int8 | 5.8 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-base-nvfp4.safetensors` | Klein Base, NVFP4 | 5.3 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_bf16.safetensors` | Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct text encoder, BF16 | 8.9 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_int8_convrot.safetensors` | Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct text encoder, int8 | 4.9 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_bf16.safetensors` | prompt upsampler, BF16 | 18.8 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_int8_convrot.safetensors` | prompt upsampler, int8 | 9.8 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_w4a8.safetensors` | prompt upsampler, w4a8 | 6.7 GB |
| `vae/flux2-vae.safetensors` | image autoencoder | 0.3 GB |

The BF16 transformer and the autoencoder are the same files as `model.safetensors` and `ae.safetensors` on the original repositories. The int8 files run on 8 GB GPUs such as the RTX 3070, and on GPUs without FP8 support (RTX 30 series and older). NVFP4 needs a Blackwell GPU.

## Download

One checkpoint, its text encoder and the autoencoder, straight into the ComfyUI model folders:

```sh
hf download black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-comfy \
  diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-int8-convrot.safetensors \
  text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_int8_convrot.safetensors \
  vae/flux2-vae.safetensors \
  text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_in
